### Scope

The triage (`5834245018`): 「build the link through the router as PR objectui#10632 does, pointing at the chat route the console declares (`/ai/NAME`); draw no link when the preview has no router. Pin the link through the real route table.」

- Reproduce first: through the real console route table, today's `/console/ai/agents/NAME/chat` resolves only to the catch-all (`RedirectWithSplash to="/"`), and as a plain anchor it ignores the `/_console` basename.
- Fix: the link is built inside the router (the basename applies) and points at the declared chat route for that agent, reusing PR objectui#10632's construction. ⛔ No second link-building helper if that PR's is reachable. With no router, no link is drawn.
- Pin: the link resolves through the real route table to the agent's chat page, not the catch-all, plus the no-router control. With teeth.

⇒ `Fixes #10640`.

### The dev's open questions — answered by the seat

1. **The console test file (`apps/console/src/__tests__/App.agentChatLink-10640.test.tsx`), A: kept.** The triage binds 「Pin the link through the real route table」, and the console's root table is not exported from `App.tsx`, so this is the only place it renders. Test only, no console source, and a new file that cannot collide. The seat extends the claim's surface to it (PR objectui#10632's console pin is the precedent).
2. **`?new=1`, A: kept.** The link's own title has always promised 「in a new chat」, and without the flag a custom agent resumes the ask-scope thread cached for the user, which may belong to another agent. It is the chat page's existing flag (the sidebar's New button uses it). Cost: one new conversation row per click, which is what the title says.
